pairs.difference: A: red bandana with white dots that give the eye a neutral place to rest. The bow knot's shadow turns a deeper red and the background is a mid cyan. B: the scarf is one pure red over its whole area, with only a gold fire badge for contrast. Its subject chroma (0.217) is above the real range, and the folds lose chroma (0.84 kept) without moving to another hue. The swirl background is pushed toward cyan, like the generated glove lessons.
pairs.fix: Make the scarf a slightly dusty cotton red, not pure red. Let the folds darken toward deep wine-purple. Make the badge a muted brass, and use a calmer blue for the background.

pairs.difference: A: coaster cars in yellow and red on a cobalt track under a blue sky. The colors are pure but the hue roles are clear, with a warm hero on a cool background. B: the wagon card is pulled warm overall (warm share 0.69, above the real range). The canvas is cream, not white, and the wood, wheels, dirt road and grass all fall into orange. Shadows under the wagon stay saturated orange-red (shadow chroma kept 1.22), the same sameness seen in the generated computer and glove lessons.
pairs.fix: Paint the canvas cover an off-white with cool grey folds. Make the wood a natural grey-brown and the wheels a barn red. Let the shadows under the wagon fall to a cool brown-violet, and add green to the grass so the ground isn't all orange.

pairs.difference: A: the orange striped background, orange sand and the cactus's cast shadow all sit in one orange family. The cactus green leans yellow, and the shadow on the sand stays a saturated orange-brown. B: green binoculars on a yellow plank floor. The barrels are dark and near-neutral, the lenses blue, and the shadows dark and only slightly warm (0.43). The card has more neutral rest.
pairs.fix: Keep the cactus a cool sage green. Make the cast shadow on the sand a muted violet-brown, not orange. Use a less saturated sand-beige for the ground so it doesn't merge with the orange backdrop.

pairs.difference: B is the real lighthouse card from the lessons: white stone with cool grey-blue shadows, a red cap and a blue sea. A: the windmill is almost colorless (subject chroma 0.037, below the real range), with cream blades and warm grey stone. Its shadow areas carry more chroma than its lit areas (1.65, above the real range): the brown shadow on the tower and the orange-gold field next to it.
pairs.fix: Make the windmill blades white-grey with cool blue-grey shade. Give the stone tower a light cool grey with soft lavender shadows, and keep the red tail vane a clean red. Paint the field a softer straw yellow.

pairs.difference: A: a single purple ring background (background chroma 0.25, above the real range) covers the card. The golden rope folds into the same mauve mass in the lens, so the card reads as about one hue family (1.3). B: a navy cap with an orange band and a gold tassel on cyan rings. The hue roles are clear, and the cap's shadows go to a deep blue-violet, much like the real camera.
pairs.fix: Use a calmer mid-violet or blue background. Make the rope a natural tan straw color with brown shadows, clearly separate from the background hue, and keep the red binding as the single accent.

pairs.difference: A: desert sand, cowboy hat, skin, pig, beans and overalls all pull warm (warm share 0.74, above the real range). Only the blue shirt and the sky break it. Hue families come to 3.9, below the real minimum, and shadows on the sand stay orange-tan. B: the pig and cow sit on a violet dusk stage with multicolor lights, which matches the real range of hue families and warm share.
pairs.fix: Pull the sand toward a pale cool beige with lavender shadows. Give the sky a deeper blue and add some green cactus and blue-grey rock so the card isn't all orange-tan.

pairs.difference: A: a tan jacket with orange cuffs, a forest-green sash and yellow badges on a green ray background. The tan shadows go to a muted brown, and the hues spread across several families. B: the cowboy hat is an orange-brown whose shadows stay saturated red-brown under the brim. It sits on a bright cyan ray background, the same pairing as the generated glove lessons (an orange object with orange shadows on a cyan burst).
pairs.fix: Make the hat a felt brown with less orange. Let the shadow under the brim go to a deep cool umber with a hint of violet, and use a deeper cobalt blue for the ray background, not bright cyan.

pairs.difference: A: the mesa, the foreground sand and the distant buttes are all orange-red. The shadow faces of the mesa stay saturated red, and only the sky is cool. Subject chroma (0.156) is just above the real range. B: a green topiary on a green lawn. It is nearly all green (warm share 0.05) with dark green shadows and a grey stone ring as a neutral.
pairs.fix: Give the mesa a muted terracotta with dusty violet shadow faces. Paint the desert floor a pale sandy beige, and add sage-green shrubs and blue-violet distant buttes.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart is red and white with gold trim, on a blue background. Red shadows go to a deep crimson-brown, and the white stripes and pavement give neutral rest. B: the horseshoe is almost colorless grey (subject chroma 0.045, below the real range). It sits on a hot pink background and orange sand, and the whole card is pulled warm (0.86, above the real range). Its shadow is a pinkish grey-violet.
pairs.fix: Make the horseshoe a cooler blue-grey steel with clear highlights, and its studs brass. Calm the background to a softer rose or a blue, and make the sand a pale beige so pink and orange don't compete.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers carry blue, neon lime, teal, hot pink, orange and lavender soles all at once. That gives 5.5 hue families, above the real maximum, with every accent at full chroma on an orange-yellow background. B: a brown leather boot with one yellow star accent on a green background. It has a clear hero-and-background split and dark brown shadows.
pairs.fix: Draw the sneakers in two colors, blue with white soles, and use a single accent color on the laces or logo. Remove the neon pink, teal and lime trims.

pairs.difference: A: a pink popsicle on a green ray background, a two-hue complementary card with pink-red shadows. B: a crimson box, cream lining, gold medal and blue ribbon on a bright cyan ray background. That gives 5.4 hue families, above the real range. The cyan center glow is like the generated glove backgrounds, and the lining is warm cream, not neutral.
pairs.fix: Make the box a deeper velvet red and its lining a neutral off-white grey. Drop the blue ribbon or tone it down, and use a deeper royal blue background with no cyan glow.

pairs.difference: A: the bird feeder has an orange roof and a yellow box on a brown tree, with tan pavement. Warm share (0.67) is at the top of the real range, and shadows inside the box stay flat orange-brown. Shadow chroma kept (0.61) is just below the real range. B: neon pink, orange and green signs against a navy night, so the hue roles are clear and the shadows stay blue-violet.
pairs.fix: Paint the feeder in natural weathered wood: a soft honey-brown box and a muted red roof. Make the shadows inside the box and under the roof a cool dark brown-violet, and give the park background more cool greens and blue.

pattern: Generated cards pull warm across the whole card. Whites turn cream, as on the computer, the lighthouse stone and the wagon canvas. Browns turn orange, as on the glove and the hat. Ground surfaces such as sand, desert, wood and dirt all fall into the same orange family as the hero. Shadows keep the lit hue at full saturation, with orange shadow on orange. Real cards shift shadows toward muted violet-brown or blue-grey, and they keep true neutral whites and greys as rest areas. Backgrounds are pushed to brighter, cyan-leaning bursts. Palettes swing to extremes: either one hue covers the whole card, or neon candy accents spread across many hue families.
